chunks: From him, from al-Abbas, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"There is no harm in praying in congregation on the ship."

key_terms.بَأْسَ: Harm or difficulty; used in the negative 'la ba'sa' to indicate permissibility or lack of objection.
key_terms.جَمَاعَةٍ: Congregation or group; referring to the collective performance of prayer.

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray in congregation on a ship according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) affirms the validity of congregational prayer on ships, addressing the practical needs of maritime travel in the early Islamic era. It underscores the flexibility of Shia jurisprudence in maintaining communal worship (*jama'ah*) even in dynamic environments, provided the basic conditions of prayer are met despite the vessel's movement.
